findings.issue: The dialog detector misses role written as a JSX expression, e.g. role={'dialog'} or role={"alertdialog"}, so a future dialog written that way would escape the source-vs-list check.
findings.evidence: DIALOG = /<dialog\b|role=["']?(alert)?dialog\b/ — 'role={"dialog"}' has '{' after '=' and does not match. A-3 only names role="dialog" so this is within spec, but it is a cheap hole in AC#2's guard.
findings.fix: Use /<dialog\b|role=\{?["']?(alert)?dialog\b/ and add one fixture row in tests/ui/play-money.test.ts.

findings.issue: The A-7 attribute list ['aria-label','aria-description','title','alt','placeholder'] is written twice (collectText and watchEnding); a later addition to one would silently skip the other.
findings.evidence: Lines 46 and 67 repeat the same literal array. Both functions run in the page via page.evaluate, so a shared module const can't be closed over directly.
findings.fix: Pass the list as the evaluate argument to both (page.evaluate(collectText, ATTRS) / page.evaluate(watchEnding, ATTRS)) from one const ACCESSIBLE_ATTRIBUTES.

findings.issue: real[\s-]?(money|cash) would flag a future disclaimer such as 'Play money only - no real money', which is the opposite of an offer.
findings.evidence: No such text exists today; it's the spec's A-1 phrase list, so the code is correct. The risk only shows up if someone later adds that wording.
findings.fix: None needed now. If such copy is added, docs/ui/play-money.md should say to phrase it differently or the rule should exclude 'no real money'.

summary: All 8 SPEC items are implemented as specified and the new tests pass (vitest 10/10; play-money.spec.ts 6/6 on Chromium and WebKit, about 1 s per walk). Test strength: the walk visits every SCREEN_LIST id, and the final visited-set assertion fails if any id is skipped or a new list entry is never visited. The ending capture resolves only when main[aria-busy="true"] appears, and only App.tsx:251 renders that. If the screen were missed, the evaluate would hang and the test would time out, so it can't pass by skipping. The source scan takes routes from the Screen union, so a new route fails SPEC-02 by name, and a removed Screen type marks every screen entry stale. The fixture test checks that both text and aria-label 'Deposit' are rejected with the exact message. The phrase list passes every play-money vocabulary row and the word-boundary cases (stripes, prepayment). Recorded deviation (hand 14 played with call so a Hand #14 review opens) is correct: playToResult supports play:'call', and the review is asserted visible before the check. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
